questions.q: Why doesn't Theo simply remove the cluster-wide average metric from the FinOps dashboard?
options: Removing it is impossible in the dashboarding tool
The average still answers a real question Finance/leadership care about — whether the cluster is sized correctly for its cost — so the fix is additive, not a replacement
Casey Lindqvist forbids removing any existing metric
The average is actually more accurate than any per-zone number
questions.explain: The average is incomplete, not wrong — it answers a real capacity/cost question. The fix adds the missing per-zone breakdown alongside it instead of deleting something still useful.

questions.q: What is the actual query change Theo makes to add the new panel?
options: Switching from Prometheus to a completely different monitoring tool
Adding a `by (zone)` grouping to the existing utilization query, so it returns one number per zone instead of one collapsed number
Increasing the dashboard's refresh rate
Rewriting the FinOps dashboard from scratch in a new framework
questions.explain: The underlying per-pod metrics were always there; grouping by the topology.kubernetes.io/zone label is the entire technical lift needed to go from one number to one number per zone.

questions.q: What would the new per-zone panel have shown during the actual incident?
options: All three zones reporting identical, healthy numbers
eastus2-2 at roughly 96% utilization sitting next to eastus2-1 and eastus2-3 at roughly 24% — the exact imbalance a manual kubectl investigation had to uncover
A single blended number with no zone detail, same as before
No data at all, since zone-level metrics didn't exist
questions.explain: The new panel surfaces the same imbalance Theo found manually in Lesson 12, now visible at a glance next to the cluster-wide average.

questions.q: What additional change does Theo push for, beyond just adding the visual panel?
options: Removing all alerting from the FinOps dashboard
Changing the alerting rule to also flag when any single zone's average is skewed well above the others, not just when the cluster-wide average crosses 80%
Deleting the reliability dashboard since it's now redundant
Lowering the cluster-wide alert threshold to 50%
questions.explain: A visual panel alone still requires someone to look at it; an alert on zone-level skew would page someone proactively the next time a similar imbalance occurs.

questions.q: What is the right scope for this fix, according to the lesson?
options: A full rebuild of the FinOps dashboard from scratch
One additive panel plus an updated alert rule — keeping the existing average metric intact
Switching the entire company to a different cloud provider
Deleting the FinOps dashboard and relying only on the reliability dashboard going forward
questions.explain: The gap was narrow and specific — no per-zone breakdown — so the right-sized fix is a new panel and a smarter alert, not a wholesale rebuild.
